0.long_answer: The deletion in question is a 4,977 base pair mitochondrial DNA deletion. This deletion, which occurs between 13 base pair repeats, is found in approximately one-third of individuals with chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia (CPEO) and is also the most common deletion associated with Kearns–Sayre syndrome. It disrupts key mitochondrial functions, leading to impaired oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production, thereby contributing to the clinical symptoms observed in these mitochondrial disorders.
